  WHY: Future cap events would produce misleading operator-facing status about whether the blocker was sent.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:{blocked_comment_posted / _contains_marker} | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]

  WHY: In unattended issue mode, a session can satisfy the check without posting on the issue and silently stall the chain at the cap.

- tests/test_unattended_question_guard.py:{around the "no subprocess" assertion} | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test forbids "subprocess", "urllib", "http.client", "requests", "socket", and "gh api" in the hook source, so it will fail when the documented #5083 follow-up intentionally adds `subprocess.run` for `gh api`.
  WHY: This forward-compatibility hazard can block the follow-up's CI despite its planned behavior being intentional and documented.

- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:{evaluate, "Cap allows the third stop" branch} | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cap message says "the stop is allowed and nothing was posted on the issue," which will be false if the planned #5083 follow-up posts the blocker.
  WHY: Future cap events would produce misleading status that operators and the session read as "no blocker was sent."

- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:{blocked_comment_posted / _contains_marker} | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The check returns True when any successful tool call in the current turn has `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` anywhere in its input, without verifying that it was a comment-posting tool, that the marker was in the comment body, or that the label was added.
  WHY: A session can dodge the §28 guard at the cap without posting on the issue, leaving the chain stalled silently.

- Requirement: "Only sessions marked unattended are affected. ... A session without CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID, or without a marker for that id, is never blocked or denied." (CLAUDE.md §28.A / §28.G body)
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md step 1 ("When the plan's header carries a Source issue: <owner>/<repo>#<N> line, run ... mark ...") plus a Project-mode guard
  Evidence of absence: Step 1 in the new implement-plan-claude.md now calls mark on every plan with a `Source issue:` line, including **project-mode** plans (which the issue mode lives in addition to project mode, see Step 2 of the same file). §28.A / §28.G scope the guard to *issue mode*, but the step-1 wording "every session of the chain" reads as a global gate. No diff hunk or test narrows the step-1 invocation to issue mode. The companion doc and the test only assert that step 1 contains the mark command; there is no test or contract that verifies the call is skipped for project-mode plans.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- Requirement: "The hook makes no GitHub API calls (§15)" (per CLAUDE.md §28.G body, the agents.md note, and the changelog fragment's "GitHub API calls from the hook | 0" row).
  Expected change site: docs/plans/issue-5083-guard-cap-source-issue-blocker-plan.md + agents.md + CLAUDE.md + changelog.d/4911-unattended-question-guard.md.
  Evidence of absence: The docs/plans/issue-5083-...-plan.md describes adding `subprocess.run` for `gh api` inside the same hook, contradicting the no-API-calls claim the same PR bakes into three separate docs. No diff hunk updates those docs to flag the conflict or marks the no-API-calls claim as "until #5083 lands." A reader of just the agents.md or changelog fragment will be misled.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
